disease_label_per_paper: Enterococcus cecorum human bacteremia with epigastric pain, diarrhea, colonic thickening, and shaking chills
presentation_summary: 80-year-old woman with major vascular history, aortic aneurysm repair, thoracic aortic aneurysm, lung cancer after lobectomy, peptic ulcer disease, COPD, coronary artery disease with stent, and ischemic colitis presented with 24 hours of intermittent epigastric pain.
The episode was associated with lightheadedness, shortness of breath, constipation, then explosive diarrhea followed by subjective fever and shaking chills.
Initial vitals were afebrile but mildly hypotensive with oxygen saturation 95% on 2 L nasal cannula; labs showed leukocytosis with neutrophil predominance and acute creatinine elevation.
CTA showed diffuse mild colonic wall thickening with liquid stool; two admission blood-culture sets later grew Enterococcus cecorum.

risk_context.source_text_value: 80-year-old woman with extensive vascular and cardiopulmonary comorbidity
history of ischemic colitis, epigastric pain, diarrhea, and diffuse mild colonic wall thickening

observations.source_text_value: intermittent epigastric pain for the past 24 hours
episode of non-bloody explosive diarrhea followed by fever and shaking chills
heart rate of 58 beats per minute
oxygen saturation of 95% on 2 L nasal cannula
shortness of breath associated with the episode
history of ischemic colitis with acute diarrhea and CT colonic wall thickening
CT imaging of the abdomen/pelvis revealed diffuse mild thickening of the colonic wall

imaging.source_text_value: CT imaging of the abdomen/pelvis revealed diffuse mild thickening of the colonic wall, considerably sparing the cecum with liquid stool throughout
no evidence of hematoma, gas, inflammation or significant change from one year prior
TTE did not reveal evidence of endocarditis

microbiology.source_text_value: both sets of blood cultures drawn on admission grew Enterococcus cecorum
stool studies were negative for Shigella, Salmonella, Aeromonas, Clostridium difficile and Campylobacter
sensitive to ampicillin and vancomycin and synergistic with streptomycin and gentamicin

confirmatory_findings.source_text_value: both blood cultures grew E. cecorum
no clear source as the patient denied poultry, domestic animal, recent travel, abnormal exposure, new skin lesions, or diet changes
repeat blood cultures drawn 48 hours after initial cultures showed no growth

actual_treatment.source_text_value: empiric coverage with piperacillin/tazobactam was started
antibiotic therapy was deescalated to IV ampicillin/sulbactam
started on oral amoxicillin on day 4 and discharged on oral amoxicillin every 12 hours for 14 days

outcome.source_text_value: leukocytosis resolved, no further diarrhea, fevers or chills; discharged home on day 5

quality_warnings: Blood-culture species and susceptibility are confirmatory/non-ranking.
GI symptom pattern, chills, vitals, leukocytosis, creatinine, and CT colonic wall thickening are presentation evidence.
